focus: Focus on the results at 2 and 4 weeks.
modelNote:
Create a clean, professional portrait infographic for a university student summarising the results-focused research paper:

Title at top: "Time Management Training: Results at 2 and 4 Weeks"
Subtitle: "Häfner, Stock & Oberst (2015) • Undergraduate students • n = 23 for main analyses"

Strictly use only the facts and numbers below. Do not add any extra facts, calculated percentages, examples, or claims. Spell everything correctly. Portrait tall layout, clear hierarchy, large readable text, simple icons and charts.

Overall style: university handout, white background, deep blue and teal accents, small orange highlight for stress. Use icons: clock, calendar, checklist, student, chart. Use simple line/bar charts with exact values from the paper.

Section 1: "Study set-up" with three timepoint icons in a horizontal timeline:
- "Time 1: directly before training"
- "Time 2: 2 weeks after"
- "Time 3: 4 weeks after"
Add small note: "4 h time management training".
Add small design note: "One trained group; demands used as a control variable expected not to change."

Section 2: "What changed after training?" Use three mini line charts across Time 1, Time 2, Time 3 using the exact means and labels:
Chart A title: "Perceived stress (tension)" y-axis label "Mean score". Values: Time 1 = 3.30, Time 2 = 2.96, Time 3 = 3.03. Use orange line descending then slight rise. Add callouts:
- At 2 weeks: "Significantly less than pretest: F(1,22)=8.22, p<0.01, partial η²=0.27"
- At 4 weeks: "Significantly less than pretest: F(1,22)=5.75, p=0.03, partial η²=0.21"

Chart B title: "Perceived control of time". Values: Time 1 = 2.75, Time 2 = 2.89, Time 3 = 3.05. Use teal line increasing. Add callouts:
- At 2 weeks: "Tendency in expected direction: F(1,22)=3.38, p=0.08, partial η²=0.13"
- At 4 weeks: "Significant increase: F(1,22)=11.62, p<0.01, partial η²=0.35"

Chart C title: "Demands (control variable)". Values: Time 1 = 3.59, Time 2 = 3.35, Time 3 = 3.46. Use gray line. Add callout:
- "No significant change: 2 weeks t(22)=1.68, p=0.107; 4 weeks t(22)=1.19, p=0.251"

Section 3: "Overall time effects" Use two compact cards:
Card 1: "Pretest vs. 2 weeks" with: "Overall time effect significant: F(2,21)=4.09, p=0.03, partial η²=0.28"
Card 2: "Pretest vs. 4 weeks" with: "Overall time effect significant: F(2,21)=6.01, p<0.01, partial η²=0.36"

Section 4: "Training transfer" with checklist icon. Text:
"Use of taught time management strategies"
- "2 weeks: nearly significant increase, t(22)=1.62, p=0.060, ε′=0.48"
- "4 weeks: significant increase, t(22)=2.67, p<0.01, ε′=0.79"
Add a small three-bar chart with exact means: Time 1 = 3.01, Time 2 = 3.19, Time 3 = 3.31. Label it "Time management behaviour".

Section 5: "Authors' interpretation" with light blue box:
"The authors conclude that the intended variables changed while demands did not, supporting the conclusion that the training led to decreased perceived stress and increased perceived control of time. They state that trainees transferred the training content to daily work at least to some extent."

Section 6: "Main caution" with warning icon:
"Preliminary study: small sample size. The authors say more intervention studies, especially with larger samples, are necessary. They also note that an experimental design with a control group or pseudo-training groups would be a methodological improvement."

Footer: "Measures named as in the paper: perceived stress = tension scale; demands = perceived, self-reported demands."

Make sure every word is spelled correctly. Keep text concise but readable. Do not include any other statistics or information.
